GERARDS---This school has a fine record, athletically, and was the nursery of Bill Curtin and Arnold Bentt. Present members continuing the tradition are John Ioannou, Stephen McFall, Mark Waight, Alan Carey and John Hickey.
High Jump: Arnold Bentt must have a magic way with bars--he did everything bar knock it down on his way to 6 feet, but this is the height he achieved.
Steve White scored a sprint double (10.5 y/22.5y) while Arnold Bentt leapt a season's best 22'-1¼" to finish 2nd in the long jump and followed up with a below par high jump (5'-7") for 6th.

Shades of Frank Simmon's at his most fearsome! Apart from these two performances, Arnold Bentt, who finished second in the high jump and our relay team should be specially mentioned.

Our winners were Bruno Hafner ('B' 100 metres), Lionel Mann ('B' 5000 metres), Alan Black ('B' steeplechase), Charlie Gillett ('B' 400 metres hurdles), Arnold Bentt ('A' High Jump), Bob Couillault ('B' Triple Jump) and the 4 x 100 metres relay team of Lee Sullivan, Bruno Hafner, Charlie Gillett and Steve White.

Arnold Bentt was only 1" away from first place in the high-jump, and clocked 17.1s. in the "B" high hurdles. Philip Gee showed what a force he is becoming over 400m., with a 51.5s. second place in the "B" 400m.
Steve also won the long jump and contributed to our 4 x 100m winning squad. Our other winners of the meeting were Charlie Gillett in the 400m hurdles and Arnold Bentt in the triple jump.

Almost everyone ran, jumped or threw in more than one event including Charlie Gillett (400m H, 400m, 4 x 100m and 4 x 400m) Arnold Bentt (110m H, long jump, pole vault, high jump, triple jump and 4 x 100m) and of course our usual one man team "Snowy" (400m H, discus, shot, 4 x 100m and 400m).

Snowy Brooks and Arnold Bentt each contributed a handy 15 points as they dashed from one event to another, the former also running in both relays where we gained maximum points, our team in the 4 x 400m being kind enough to give him a 100m lead on the last leg, allowing him a casual circuit in 57 seconds!
The happy-go-lucky Arnold Bentt, whose all-round ability on the field earns us many valuable points.

Mick Marshall seemed to pop up everywhere, scoring well in events in which we do not usually see him. And Arnold Bentt, well, at one time his name was being called at either end of the stadium for the High Jump and Pole Vault.

After a bright start our lack of depth began to tell and despite great efforts from many people, especially Snowy Brooks, Charlie Gillett, Steve White and Arnold Bentt, we gradually slipped behind Mitcham and it looked as though we would have to settle for second place.
Hopkins in the Pole Vault, and Arnold Bentt and Reg. teamed up together again in the short hurdles and the High Jump. We rely heavily upon these two willing characters.

Other highlights included Cliff Brooks' throwing and easy 400 metre hurdles win, Arnold Bentt's triple jump of bang on 13 metres, and a determined recovery by Alan Black after he had fallen very heavily at one of the barriers in the steeplechase whilst starting to pull away from the field.
Youngsters, David Didino for example, are beginning to make their mark, and it is even rumoured that Arnold Bentt is going to train this winter.

Belated congratulations to ARNOLD BENTT and PAT on their engagement. Pat has supported us at several of our league fixtures and is already used to the strange ways of athletes, her brother being Herne Hill's talented javelin thrower Neville Wade.
Laurie O'Hara and Bill Kerr, our dependable veteran duo, again did their stuff in the 1500m and Arnold Bentt, back after an illness, proved yet again that lack of training means nothing to him.

Only three athletes contested the jumps but there were no easy victories. The Triple saw Steve Crosbie scrape home by a centimetre from Arnold Bentt but Reg. Hopkins had the advantage in the High and Long Jumps.
Cliff, Arnold Bentt and the Crosbie brothers have all had more than their share of injuries this summer but luckily they have not been kept out of action all together.
The other first places came from Reg Hopkins and Arnold Bentt in the jumps and Jamie Stevenson in the 800m. Reg also set his best ever time in the 200m.
Star of the Belgrave team for the afternoon was Arnold Bentt who suddenly and for no apparent reason added a "Beamon-like" improvement to his previous best triple jump.

Linda Nicholls writes in this issue of her stay with a Swedish club which regularly goes out into the countryside to camp and train together. Arnold Bentt, in "Spotlight", harks back to the days when we had a group of successful jumpers all working at their events together.
Belated congratulations to two Belgravians who have taken the marital plunge. Howard Satchell (can he really be 20 years a member) has married Chris from Canada, and Arnold Bentt has married Pat.
